title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwriting is on the back of a recycled typescript; the neighbouring pages are typed notes on holomorphic functions and the Cauchy theorem, unrelated to the handwritten text. The handwritten fragment belongs to the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' material. I read the recurring name as 'Deuring', not 'Deming'. Max Deuring's 'Algebren' is the classical reference for maximal orders, and he studied endomorphism rings of elliptic curves as orders in quaternion algebras.

Top lines (end of a previous paragraph). 'La catégorie des équivalences de [?] C' (C' étant de Deuring) est une Tens-catégorie sous la Gr-catégorie précédente.' The category of (Morita) equivalences of such categories is a tensor category over a categorical group (a 'Gr-catégorie', i.e. a 2-group). This is the framework of tensor categories, gerbes and bands that Grothendieck was building for the Galois theory of motives.

Ex. 1, the definition. Let A be a Dedekind ring with fraction field K and E a finite-dimensional semisimple K-algebra. One definition of a 'Deuring category of type E' over A is a category equivalent to P(O/A) = P(O/centre(O)): finitely generated projective modules (lattices) over a maximal A-order O of E. Two remarks underlie this.
- The category does not depend on the base, A or the centre of O.
- It does not depend, up to equivalence, on the choice of maximal order. Any two maximal orders are linked by an invertible connecting bimodule, so they are Morita equivalent.

Base change. The notion is compatible with extensions A -> A' (A' a field or a Dedekind ring) that are 'résiduellement fidèles', for example localisations and completions. The marked exception is étale localisations ('!!'). This is correct, and probably the point of the '!!'. Maximality of an order is stable under localisation and completion. It is not stable under unramified extension. Example: the maximal order Δ of the quaternion division algebra over Q_p, tensored with Z_{p^2}, gives a hereditary non-maximal (Iwahori-type) order in M_2(Q_{p^2}). So 'Deuring categories' defined via maximal orders do not form an étale stack. The natural étale-stable notion would be hereditary orders.

Autoequivalences. If E is central over K, the Gr-category (2-group) Aut(C) of autoequivalences of a Deuring category C of type E is claimed to have:
- π_0 = 1, on the grounds that invertible O-bimodules are trivial;
- π_1 = A^*.
The marginal note generalises the second claim. For E semisimple, π_1 = Z^*, where Z is the integral closure of A in the centre of E (equal to the centre of O). π_1 is Aut(id_C), the units of the centre of the category, i.e. Z(O)^*.

Purpose. This computes the band/2-group controlling integral forms ('catégories de Deuring') of semisimple K-linear categories. It is presumably input for integral or arithmetic versions of the motivic Galois formalism, such as endomorphism algebras of motives and their maximal orders.
errors: π_0 = 1 is false in general. The A-linear Morita autoequivalences of P(O) are classified by Picent(O), the invertible O-bimodules centralising A. For a maximal order over a Dedekind ring, Fröhlich/Reiner show Picent(O) contains a contribution from Cl(A) and local cyclic factors Z/m_p at primes where E ramifies (m_p the local index). Over a complete DVR with E a division algebra of index m, the radical P (with P^m = πO) gives a nontrivial autoequivalence of order m. Grothendieck struck out 'Si A est local', but even the local case fails unless E is split (or A is strictly henselian). The claim holds e.g. for E = M_n(K) with A local, or for A strictly henselian.
The parenthetical justification ('les bimodules sur O inversibles des deux côtés [le groupe] est trivial') is therefore inaccurate as stated.
The π_1 claims are correct: Aut(id) = Z(O)^* = Z^*, with Z the integral closure of A in the centre of E; this equals A^* when E is central.

ideas.what: Category of lattices over a maximal order as the canonical integral model ('Deuring category of type E') of the semisimple category mod-E; independent of the choice of maximal order by Morita equivalence via connecting ideals
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence of maximal orders; integral forms of semisimple categories

ideas.what: Maximal orders are stable under localisation and completion but not under étale/unramified base change
ideas.modern_name: Base change of maximal vs hereditary orders

ideas.what: Autoequivalences of such a category form a Gr-category (2-group) with π_1 = units of the integral closure of A in the centre of E, and π_0 the Picard group of invertible bimodules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bass (Picard group of rings), Fröhlich 1973 (Picard groups of orders); Sinh 1975 (Gr-categories)
ideas.where_published: Gr-categories appear in Grothendieck's circle (Sinh's thesis, Giraud); not in this form in his published texts

ideas.what: Equivalences of Deuring categories forming a tensor category over the 2-group of autoequivalences
ideas.modern_name: Morita 2-category / gerbe of integral forms (Brauer-type theory over A)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a notion of integral 'Deuring categories of type E' (A-models of semisimple categories via maximal orders) as part of an integral/arithmetic Tannakian theory for motives. He notes that it fails to be stable under étale localisation. The natural repair (hereditary orders, or a stack built from them) and the classification of such categories via gerbes banded by the 2-group computed here are not carried out.
missed.quote: complétions — mais [pas?] les localisations étales !! ... la Gr-catégorie des équivalences d'une C de Deuring de type E a un π_0 = 1 ... il vient le π_1 = A^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of motivic or Tannakian categories (e.g. integral motives, orders in endomorphism algebras of abelian varieties) remain an active theme. This page shows Grothendieck already thinking of a 2-group/gerbe classification of integral forms in 1965-ish. However, the content is covered by standard order theory (Reiner, Fröhlich), and the π_0 claim is wrong in general.

deep.surprise_reason: A sketchy draft applying 2-group/gerbe language to categories of lattices over maximal orders, with a correct observation on étale base change and a mistaken π_0 claim. Historically mildly interesting as a glimpse of integral Tannakian ideas in the motives notes, but the mathematics itself is standard (Morita theory of orders, Picent).
transcription_corrections: 'Deming'/'Dennin' is very likely 'Deuring' (catégories de Deuring), after Max Deuring's theory of maximal orders.
'Tens-catégorie' and 'Gr-catégorie' readings appear correct (tensor category; categorical group).
'ass. semi-simples' = 'associatives semi-simples'; 'finie' inserted: 'algèbres finies associatives semi-simples E sur K'.
'c.a.d. résiduelles les fidèles' is probably 'c.à.d. résiduellement fidèles' (or similar).
'mais les localisations étales !!' is possibly 'mais pas les localisations étales !!'; this reading is mathematically apt, since maximality is not preserved under unramified extension.
First line: 'équivalences de Coxeter' is doubtful; probably 'équivalences de Morita' or similar referring to equivalences of the category C'.

Margin: 'Z^*' (units of Z), Z = 'clôture intégrale de A dans le centre de E'; last line '(Donc si E central sur K, π_1 = A^*)'. The image seems to read 'central sur A' or 'K'; in any case meaning centre of E equal to K.
